newsitem.title: GERMANY: Global 96/97 butter output at 5.67 mln T-Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Global 96/97 butter output at 5.67 mln T-Oil World.

text.p: World butter production in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) looks set to be slightly up from last season at 5.67 million tonnes, Oil World newsletter said.
This level, although higher than 5.64 million tonnes recorded in 95/96 -- compared with 6.1-6.5 million tonnes seen in the late 1980s and early 1990s, the independent publication said.
This was a result of European Union production curbs and sharp falls in former communist eastern bloc output since 1989.
Russian and Ukrainean output in the present season was still being reduced and in the EU, larger parts of available milk volumes were going into other uses.
But butter output in the United States and India was forecast to rise and the same applied to Oceania, namely New Zealand.
Consumption in 96/97 was forecast at 5.70 million tonnes compared with 5.60 million in 95/96.
Oil World said global 96/97 imports would rise to 597,00 tonnes from 493,000 tonnes, led by Russia, which might buy 138,000 tonnes versus 61,000 tonnes last season.
Egypt, Morocco and South Africa were also notable importers. Export supplies came from New Zealand, the EU, and Australia.
